purpose: Establish a repeatable anonymous fetch path for documentation observed in the linked-source review, so that it can be ingested by the bounded source worker.
method: Anonymous HTTPS GET with an identifying User-Agent, about one request per second, no credentials, redirects not followed. Bodies were inspected transiently in a local temp directory for format discovery and were not committed, stored in MongoDB, embedded, or uploaded to Azure AI Search. robots.txt was evaluated with an RFC 9309 matcher that supports * and $ wildcards (the Python standard-library parser does not).

findings.finding: Product pages are a client-rendered Nuxt shell. They are a catalog source, not a documentation source.
findings.action: Do not fetch product pages for content.

findings.finding: Knowledge-base search links render a login page with HTTP 200.

The documentation portal is an Angular single-page app whose HTML has no article text. The SPA loads anonymous JSON: /daily/prodandaddon.json (product directory), /{ns}/{version}/tocflat.json (table of contents with href and revisionId), and /{href}/default-{revisionId}.json (page HTML in parse.text['*']). The user-facing citation URL is /doc/{href}. Adding /doc/ to the JSON paths returns an S3 AccessDenied 403, which is a wrong path rather than an authentication response. JSON responses carry ETag and Last-Modified.
findings.robots: robots.txt allows the selected paths; it disallows */beta/*, */itomw/*, */classic/*, */admin/*, *&action=* and selected ITOM namespaces. A sitemap index is published.

findings.finding: Help pages are server-rendered HTML with the topic body in #mc-main-content. robots.txt lists per-product sitemaps (lr, lre, valueedge) and disallows older versions and some PDFs. HTML responses carry ETag and Last-Modified.
findings.action: Use kind sitemap, filtered to the current version path.

findings.finding: The legal and terms page returned HTTP 403 to an automated fetch.
findings.action: Source terms remain unverified and require a manual review.
